audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) The shield is credited to his passive ('Grit passive gives him a free shield every fight', 'his Grit shield'). (b) Knuckle Down is called a slow in three places. (c) The Show Stopper is called a suppression that 'cancels your E dash on reaction'.
audit.why: Pit Grit is alternating left/right punches plus missing-health regeneration — no shield. Grit is stored on Haymaker and only becomes a shield when he casts W. Knuckle Down gives his next two attacks max-health damage and move speed toward champions; there is no slow in Riot's text. The Show Stopper's text is a carry-and-slam with a landing slow, 400 range — suppression and dash-cancel priority are not stated anywhere in the kit. Facebreaker also only stuns when it catches enemies on opposite sides of him; one side is a slow, which is the actual thing to play around at 425 range.
audit.corrected: Shield moved from the passive to the Haymaker cast; the Knuckle Down slow replaced with max-health damage on two punches; the suppression/dash-cancel replaced with the 400-range slam; Facebreaker's opposite-sides stun condition stated.

edits.before: Sett's level-1 Grit shield and heavy autos turn your trades against you.
edits.after: Sett's Pit Grit regen and alternating punches beat your level-1 trades.

edits.before: At 2 his auto pressure and shield keep him ahead in every exchange.
edits.after: At 2 his punch pressure and stored Grit keep him ahead in exchanges.

edits.before: Level 3 Knuckle Down slow into Facebreaker pins you for his combo.
edits.after: Level 3 Knuckle Down max-HP punches into Facebreaker pin you.

edits.before: Sett's Haymaker (W) stores your damage into a grey-health true-damage punch, so the harder you burst him the harder he hits back; his Knuckle Down (Q) slow plus Grit shield make him win every extended trade at this stage.
edits.after: Sett's Haymaker (W) banks the damage you deal as Grit and spends it as a shield plus a true-damage punch, so the harder you burst the harder he swings back; Knuckle Down (Q) adds max-health damage to his next two hits.

edits.before: At 6 The Show Stopper (R) suppresses and displaces you before you can line up Purgatory; his Grit shield keeps him topped up, so he rarely drops into your totem's execute threshold in a fair fight.
edits.after: At 6 The Show Stopper (R) carries and slams you from 400 range before you line up Purgatory; his Haymaker shield keeps him topped up, so he rarely drops into your totem's execute threshold.

edits.before: With his first bruiser item Sett's Haymaker punch and W shield make him a brick — your W-and-E burst feeds his stored grey health, and his R suppress can cancel your all-in on reaction.
edits.after: With his first bruiser item Sett's Haymaker punch and its shield make him a brick — your W-and-E burst just feeds his Grit, and his 400-range R answers the moment your all-in lands.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 Sett wins the lane: Grit passive gives him a free shield every fight and his auto attacks hit hard, so your Silver Stake on-hit trades come back on you worse. Worse, dumping damage into him charges Haymaker (W). Farm at range, don't feed his W, and only step up when his Grit shield is spent.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 Sett wins the lane: his alternating punches hit hard and Pit Grit regenerates harder the lower he drops, so your on-hit trades come back on you worse. Worse, dumping damage into him charges Haymaker (W) into a shield. Farm at range, don't feed his W, and only step up once he has spent his Grit.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 he controls the trades. Knuckle Down (Q) slows you into his Facebreaker (E) pull, and his stored Haymaker punches for true damage scaled off the burst you just did — so your all-in literally arms his counter. His shield keeps him healthy, so he rarely drops to a threatenable level. Play safe and look for jungle help rather than solo trades.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 he controls the trades. Knuckle Down (Q) loads max-health damage onto two punches and speeds him at you, Facebreaker (E) only stuns if it catches you and a minion on opposite sides, and Haymaker returns the burst you just dealt as true damage — so your all-in arms his counter. Play safe and look for jungle help rather than solo trades.

edits.before: Post-items Sett is a wall that punishes commitment. Your W-and-E burst pours into his grey-health W and comes back as a true-damage haymaker, while The Show Stopper (R) suppresses you and cancels your E dash on reaction. Don't full-commit into him — poke, disengage, and only engage when his W and R are down or catch him repositioning in fights.
edits.after: Post-items Sett is a wall that punishes commitment. Your W-and-E burst pours into his Grit and comes back as a shield plus a true-damage haymaker, while The Show Stopper (R) picks you up and slams you out of position. Don't full-commit into him — poke, disengage, and only engage when his W and R are down or catch him repositioning in fights.

edits.after: The Show Stopper (R) baited out before you all-in

notes: Knuckle Down has no slow in Riot's text — it is max-health damage on two attacks plus move speed toward champions; the page asserted the slow three times. Sett's shield comes from casting Haymaker with stored Grit, not from his passive. I removed the 'R suppresses and cancels your E dash' claim rather than restating it: neither suppression nor dash-cancel priority appears in the kit files and I could not verify it.
